title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
formal: For every fixed integer \(\Delta\ge1\), is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for integer linear optimization \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\), on inputs for which every square submatrix of A has determinant of absolute value at most Delta?
definitions:
The matrix A is integral with m rows and n columns, and b and c are integral vectors of lengths m and n. All entries, signs and dimensions are explicitly encoded in binary; L is the total input bit length. Every square submatrix of each size 1 through min(m,n) is covered by the determinant promise, including singular submatrices. There is no restriction on the number of nonzero entries per row or column, and n is not fixed.

For each fixed Delta the algorithm must run in at most C_Delta (L+1)^{k_Delta} bit operations for constants depending only on Delta. Thus this is a polynomial-time question for each fixed parameter value, not a strongly polynomial or fixed-parameter-tractable running-time requirement. Correctness is only required on promised matrices; recognizing the promise is not part of the task. The output is INFEASIBLE if no integral feasible point exists, UNBOUNDED if feasible objective values have no lower bound, and otherwise an integral feasible minimizer and its exact objective value. The vectors and values use binary encodings.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithmic existence proof for every fixed Delta with the stated bit-time bounds and all three outcomes, or refute it. An algorithm with an additional row-sparsity restriction or fixed dimension does not settle the question; any assumption-based obstruction must be stated conditionally.
context: Bounded determinants generalize important tractable matrix classes. The unrestricted-dimensional question remains broader than results exploiting sparsity.
why: This asks whether a bounded departure from total unimodularity guarantees tractable integer optimization.

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
import_provenance.original_statement: For every fixed Δ, can arbitrary integer linear programs min{cᵀx:Ax≤b, x∈ℤⁿ} be solved in polynomial time when every square subdeterminant of the integer matrix A has absolute value at most Δ? Weismantel and coauthors’ bimodular algorithm handles Δ≤2; the question allows zero determinants and unrestricted row sparsity.

The matrix may be dense and the number of variables grows with the input.
The target is polynomial bit complexity for each fixed determinant bound.
